subject: zero.cell.warn - when are empty cells in a bivariate table an issue?

messages.author: 5dadf4dbf792b603
messages.subject: zero.cell.warn - when are empty cells in a bivariate table an issue?
parts:
Dear all,

I noticed that since I use the new lavaan version ( version 0.5-17) , I get many warnings regarding empty cells in the bivariate tables.

(When) do I need to be concerned about such warnings? and what are remedies?

In the current case, my N = 1686
9 items, all 6 point-Likert scale
and I got 50+ warnings about empty cells when I fitted a bifactor model and used the categorical data option.

best,
Michael

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: zero.cell.warn - when are empty cells in a bivariate table an issue?
parts:
On 10/09/2014 09:38 PM, Michael Paul Grosz wrote:
> Dear all,
>
> I noticed that since I use the new lavaan version ( version 0.5-17) , I
> get many warnings regarding empty cells in the bivariate tables.

> (When) do I need to be concerned about such warnings? and what are remedies?

It depends. They are warnings, not errors. But it doesn't hurt to have a
look at some of these bivariate frequency tables. You can use the
lavTables() function for that. (or you can use use table() with two of
your variables)

If only one or two cells (out of 36) are empty, that is probably nothing
to worry about. But if you have many empty cells in a single table, it
gets harder to estimate the polychoric correlation for that table.

In that case, you can either treat the data as continuous (for 6-point
likert scales, this may be a reasonable approach), or collapse some
categories, and create, say 4-point scales for some or all the items.

Yves.

parts:
On 11/17/2014 03:39 PM, Seongho Bae wrote:
> How can I collapse categories 6 point to 4 points

A <- c(1,1,1,2,2,2,3,3,3,4,4,4,5,5,5,6,6,6,6)

# collapse: 1 and 2 become 1
B <- ifelse(A == 2, 1, A)

Yves.
